message.content:
Sure! If you’re looking to see the current time from the Command Prompt (or PowerShell), there’s a quick way:

```powershell
Get-Date -Format "HH:mm:ss"
```

Or, from plain CMD:

```batch
@echo off
for /f %%a in ('wmic OS Get localdatetime ^| find "."') do set ldt=%%a
set hh=%ldt:~8,2%
set mm=%ldt:~10,2%
set ss=%ldt:~12,2%
echo Current Time: %hh%:%mm%:%ss%
```

If you simply want to display the time right away without scripting, type this into CMD:

```batch
TIME /T
```

That will print something like:

```
13:45
```

(Your exact output will depend on your computer’s clock.)
